name: Herald of Purity resets Justice's cooldown at its own tooltip chance (#9129)
contract: Herald of Purity 806058's tooltip reads 'Damage dealt by Justice now has an 8% chance to reset its own cooldown.' aura_ascension_sun_cleric_event::Check (AscensionSunClericEvents.cpp) gated case 806058 on `info->SpellFamilyFlags[2] == 134217728`, but Justice's root spell 520359 (Spell.dbc) carries its matching family flag bit (8388608) in SpellFamilyFlags word 0, with word 2 always 0, so the comparison could never match any Justice rank and the chance roll (spell_proc Chance 0, deferring to DBC ProcChance 8 per rev_20260919_20_coa_proc_chance_parity.sql) never executed; the fix compares against `Named(info,520359)`, the chain-root helper every other case in this switch uses, so any rank of Justice (520359, 520746...572848) is recognized. aura_proc_rate replays the aura's full proc decision (db filters, conditions, script CheckProc and the native chance roll) 40000 times on a synthetic PROC_FLAG_DONE_SPELL_MELEE_DMG_CLASS hit naming Justice rank 520747 as the trigger spell, without needing a live weapon-equipped cast loop; direct = !periodic && !automatic holds for that type_mask, matching Check's own classification. Before the fix this reads 0%; the fixed comparison restores the tooltip's 8%, six-plus standard deviations inside an 8 +/- 1.5 point window at this sample size. The cast spell 520359 only triggers the damaging Justice spells 524857 and 572040, which are outside the cast rank chain and are what the proc sees as damage dealt by Justice, so the gate also accepts them (idIsJustice); the assertions with those trigger spells read 0% when only the cast chain is matched (#10831). Real casts: Justice 520359 has an 8 sec category cooldown, and aura_proc_rate never reaches the 806058 handler that clears it (Reduce(player,520359,INT32_MAX) in AscensionSunClericEvents.cpp). With Valkyr's Grip and two two-handed polearms equipped, each cast lands the main-hand strike 524857 and the off-hand strike 572040, two independent 8% rolls. The cleric attempts Justice every 1650 ms for 270 attempts without clearing the cooldown by hand, so only every fifth attempt (8250 ms after the previous completed cast) finds the cooldown elapsed and completes: with no reset exactly 54 casts complete. A reset lets the next attempt complete 1650 ms later instead of 8250 ms, so a completed-cast count of 55 or more proves the handler cleared the cooldown; a build whose handler never runs stays at 54, and 54 casts of two rolls each at 8% miss every reset with probability about 0.012%.
